ch12:label: Chapter 12
ch12:title: The Origin and Destiny of the Soul
ch12:0: The first three chapters of Part Three examined in turn the three gifts man receives. Personality comes from the Father, mind from the Infinite Spirit, and the Thought Adjuster again from the Father. Yet all three are given. There is only one reality that man acquires for himself through experience, and that is the soul. The Foreword explains the birth of the soul in terms of parent and child.
ch12:2: The soul is born with the Adjuster as father and the mind as mother, on the occasion of human choice. This chapter asks what the soul is, why it comes into being, when it is born, how it grows, and where it goes beyond death. The doctrine of the soul is the conclusion of Part Three and the foundation on which the doctrines of salvation and eternal life, to be treated in Part Six, will stand.
ch12:3: 1. Definition: A New Reality, Neither Material nor Spiritual
ch12:4: The soul is neither a part of the mind nor another name for the Adjuster. Paper 111, section 2, “Nature of the Soul,” emphasizes that the soul is not a simple sum of two factors.
ch12:6: Just as mixing water and oil produces no third substance, so placing mind and spirit side by side does not produce a soul. The soul is something new, born of the relationship between the two. The revelator therefore says that the antecedent factors of the soul are not two but three.

ch12:7.cap: Table 12.1  The Three Antecedent Factors of the Soul
rows: That mind and all the cosmic influences antecedent thereto
The Adjuster with all its inherent potentials and all spiritual influences
A value found in neither one; neither material nor spiritual, but morontial

ch12:8: The third factor is the soul itself. The midway creatures have called this soul the ‘mid-mind,’ because it lies between the material mind and the cosmic mind (111:2.8). The same section finds the reason this mid-mind can come into being in two urges of mind.
ch12:10: Man longs to know God, and God longs to know man. The soul grows at the meeting point of these two longings. The soul is the way by which man ascends to God and the way by which God gains the experience of man. The word ‘morontia’ points to precisely this in-between realm. The Foreword says, “The warp of morontia is spiritual; its woof is physical” (0:5.12). The soul is a fabric in which a warp that descends from above and a woof that rises from below are woven together.
ch12:12: 2. The Ground: Why the Soul Is Needed
ch12:13: Why does man need a soul? The answer emerges when the conclusions of the earlier chapters are brought together. Personality does not change (Chapter 9). Neither does the Adjuster change (Chapter 11). But man must grow, and life on earth ends with the body. Between these two changeless realities there must be something that grows.
ch12:15: The soul is the ever-growing relationship between the changeless personality and the changeless Adjuster. And that relationship becomes the vehicle that continues even when the body dies. The body and the material mind end on earth, but the soul becomes the new dwelling place of personality beyond death. Not every mind, however, gives rise to a soul. Animals have mind but no soul. Paper 111 names two conditions that make this possible only in the human mind.
ch12:17: The first condition is the personality of Chapter 9; the second is the ministry of the spirit of worship and the cosmic mind seen in Chapter 10. In a mind that has personality and is in contact with superanimal realities, a moral nature arises, and that moral nature effects a creative contact with the Adjuster (111:2.9). Paper 111 therefore says that the birth of a soul is the “inevitable result” of such a spiritualization of the mind.
ch12:19: This sentence contains everything needed for the soul to come into being: the adjutant mind (Chapter 10), the human will that craves to know God (Chapter 9), and the Mystery Monitor (Chapter 11). The soul is the fruit of all the realities seen in Part Three working together.
ch12:20: 3. Birth: The Moment of the First Moral Decision
ch12:21: When is the soul born? At Ephesus, when a Greek thinker asked him what the soul is, Jesus answered as follows. His answer begins by distinguishing the soul from self-consciousness.
ch12:23: Knowing oneself is not enough to make a soul. Knowing oneself in the presence of right and wrong, that is, moral self-consciousness, is the foundation of the soul. The moment the soul is born therefore coincides with the moment the Adjuster comes. In the same discourse Jesus said that the divine spirit “arrives simultaneously with the first moral activity of the human mind, and that is the occasion of the birth of the soul” (133:6.5). As we saw in Chapter 11, the Adjuster comes after the first moral decision, so the arrival of the Adjuster and the birth of the soul are two sides of the same event. And even the newborn soul is already a real entity. Paper 16 says, “From its earliest inception the soul is real; it has cosmic survival qualities” (16:9.2). The soul does not have to grow to a certain point before it becomes a soul.

ch12:24.cap: Table 12.2  The Soul as Jesus Described It at Ephesus
rows: The self-reflective, truth-discerning, and spirit-perceiving part of man
When the spirit arrives with the first moral activity of the mind
The self-realization of the moral consciousness, spiritualized and possessed of survival value
Neither science nor spirit-testing can prove it, but the moral mortal knows it by experience

ch12:25: The last item is important. The soul cannot be confirmed by a microscope or by spiritual proof. Yet Jesus said that every morally conscious mortal knows of the existence of his soul “as a real and actual personal experience” (133:6.7). Before it is an object of argument, the soul is a fact of experience.
ch12:26: 4. Growth: A Soul That Grows by Values
ch12:27: The soul, once born, grows. But the soul does not act directly on the material level; it grows between the mind and the Adjuster, becoming ever more conscious of both.
ch12:29: On the question of what the soul feeds on, Paper 111 distinguishes between meanings and values. Mind is the organ that knows, but the soul grows through what is felt.
ch12:31: The growth of the soul, then, is not proportional to the amount of knowledge. The soul grows when truth, beauty, and goodness are felt and chosen as values. The revelator says that the mortal career, the soul's evolution, “is not so much a probation as an education” (111:3.5). And he describes the cumulative result of that education in these words.
ch12:33: As the soul grows, the center of the person also shifts. On earth the power of choice resides at first in the material mind, but with time it passes over to the side of the soul.
ch12:35: The gradual shift of what a person regards as himself, from the body and the material mind to the soul, is the inner face of spiritual growth. The progress through the seven psychic circles seen in Chapter 11 also points to this process. The revelator says that the appearance of the morontia soul indicates the extent and depth of circle conquest (110:6.9).

ch12:36.cap: Table 12.3  The Four Realities in Man and Their Relation to the Soul
rows: Mother of the soul; the loom that carries the morontia fabrics; partially conscious of the soul
Father of the soul; threads in the spirit patterns; fully conscious of the soul
The power of choice, resident in the material mind during life, becomes increasingly identified with the soul
The embryo of the future morontia vehicle of personality identity

ch12:38: The soul grows, but it does not become eternal of itself. The destiny of the soul remains open to human choice to the very end. At the same time, the evolution of the soul, once begun, is not halted by human mistakes alone.
ch12:40: Where, then, do the conflicts that trouble the soul come from? In the Ephesus discourse Jesus pointed to their root: “All forms of soul conflict consist in the lack of harmony between the moral, or spiritual, self-consciousness and the purely intellectual self-consciousness” (133:6.6). When what one knows and what is right diverge, the soul is shaken. What resolves that divergence is not more knowledge but the decision to choose what is right.
ch12:41: Mistakes only slow the soul; they cannot kill it. The only thing that halts the soul is the will's choice to reject survival itself. Does the life of one who fails to survive, then, leave nothing behind? Paper 16 answers that it does not.
ch12:43: Values do not vanish. What vanishes is the identity of the ‘I’ that bore those values. The same section makes this clear: “Personality identity survives in and by the survival of the soul” (16:9.3). The question of survival is not the preservation of values but the preservation of identity, and what carries that identity is the soul. Nor do the judges of the universe settle this choice in haste. Paper 112 says that all will creatures are “to experience one true opportunity to make one undoubted, self-conscious, and final choice” (112:5.9). The destiny of the soul is determined not by chance or accident but by genuine choice.

ch12:44.cap: Table 12.4  What Remains in Survival and in Nonsurvival
rows: Survives in the survival of the soul (16:9.3)
Preserved in the soul and the Adjuster (111:3.7)
Survive as part of the continuing experience of the Adjuster (16:9.3)
Carried on into a new ascending personality (110:7.4)
Persist as a factor in the personality of the Supreme Being (16:9.3)
The Adjuster continues, bearing the experience (16:9.3)

ch12:46: At death the body and the material mind break down. But there is something that does not break down. Paper 112, section 5, “Survival of the Human Self,” names it plainly.
ch12:48: Between death and repersonalization the soul rests, unconscious, in the keeping of the seraphic destiny guardian (112:5.13). Then, on the mansion worlds, when the Adjuster returns and the soul is bestowed with a new morontia form, the person awakens again as the same personality. Here it becomes clear why Paper 111 calls the soul “the embryo of the future morontia vehicle of personality identity” (111:3.2). The soul that has grown on earth becomes the person's new body in the next world. Paper 112 sums up what continues and what changes in this transition.
ch12:50: Even on earth a person's body and mind change a little every day, yet he remains the same person. Death merely brings about that change all at once; the principle is the same. Because there is a changeless personality and a soul that has grown, the same person awakens beyond even the most sudden change.
ch12:52: The journey of the soul does not end on the mansion worlds. The soul is at first wholly morontial, but it ascends to the true spirit level (111:3.3) and at last fuses with the Adjuster. That fusion signalizes the fact that the ascending mortal “has eternally and unreservedly chosen to do the Father's will” (111:3.1). The ascension after death is taken up again in Chapter 26.

ch12:53.cap: Table 12.5  The Chain of Logic in the Doctrine of the Soul
rows: A morontia reality, neither material nor spiritual, born of the relationship between mind and spirit
A growing relationship is needed between the changeless personality and the changeless Adjuster
When the Adjuster arrives with the first moral activity
Grows by the values of truth, beauty, and goodness; a process of education
Mistakes only delay, but the will can reject survival
The morontia vehicle of personality that survives death; fusion with the Adjuster

ch12:54: In Closing: The One Thing Man Acquires for Himself
ch12:55: To close Part Three by threading the doctrine of the soul together once more: personality, mind, and the Adjuster are given, but the soul is acquired. With the mind as mother and the Adjuster as father, the soul is born in the relationship between mind and spirit as a morontia reality, neither material nor spiritual. Its birth is the moment of the first moral decision, and its growth comes through the values of truth, beauty, and goodness. Mistakes only slow the soul, but a will that rejects survival can halt it. And the surviving soul goes on beyond death to become the new vehicle of personality, on the way to becoming one with the Adjuster. Having seen the structure of man, Part Four will examine how such beings appeared on this planet and what history they have traveled.

ch12:56.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If the soul rests not on self-consciousness but on moral self-consciousness (133:6.5), which of the decisions I made today helped my soul to grow?
2. How does the saying “Mind knows quantity, reality, meanings. But quality—values—is felt” (111:3.6) show the difference between knowing and growing?
3. If the mortal career is “not so much a probation as an education” (111:3.5), how should I look upon the failures I am experiencing now?

ch13:label: Chapter 13
ch13:title: The First Human Beings and Their Family
ch13:0: Part Four reads the human history of a single planet, Urantia, as doctrine. In The Urantia Book the history of mankind is no chronicle of chance events. It is the story of a plan that planted and nurtured life, of the setbacks that shook that plan, and of a recovery that went on even in the midst of those setbacks. This chapter takes up the first link in that chain: when and how did man become man? What is the threshold between animal and human, and what did the first two beings to cross it, Andon and Fonta, leave to the human race?
ch13:1: 1. The Early Will of a Life-Experiment Planet
ch13:2: The Urantia Book places the appearance of man within the plan of the Life Carriers. The Life Carriers are the beings who plant life on a planet and watch over its evolution, and Urantia was assigned to them as a life-experiment world, a place for testing modifications of the standard life designs (65:4.1). Experiment here does not mean that things were left to take their own course. The revelator carefully limits the meaning of the word.
ch13:4: To experiment is to seek better variations on the basis of life designs already established. On Urantia the Life Carriers perfected at least twenty-eight modifications of life, and these are to be used throughout all Nebadon (65:4.1). The price of this work was the appearance of transitional forms of life that seem meaningless (65:4.10). And the greatest goal they aimed at in this experiment was the early appearance of human will.
ch13:6: This one passage is the key to the whole chapter. On Urantia the Andonic peoples appeared before the six colored races, and those six races were later born all at once from a single family (65:4.7). That human history here began in a different order from that of other worlds becomes the starting point of every peculiarity in Urantia's history, from the late arrival of the Planetary Prince (65:4.8) to the dispersion of the races and the mission of Adam. Until the Planetary Prince came, this early humanity was watched over by twelve Melchizedek receivers, who arrived when Andon and Fonta made the decisions that rendered them capable of Adjuster indwelling (65:4.9). From the very beginning, the themes of will and decision stand at the center of human history.

ch13:7.cap: Table 13.1  Distinctive Features of the Urantia Life Experiment
rows: After the colored races have long existed, usually among the red man
One by one, by independent mutations of the animal stock
Six races at once from one Sangik family
About the time human will first appears
Almost five hundred thousand years later, along with the Sangik races

ch13:9: The immediate ancestors of man came from a lemur type of placental mammal about one million years ago through three successive sudden mutations (62:0.1). This line, running from the dawn mammals to the mid-mammals and from the mid-mammals to the Primates, crossed the threshold in a pair of twins born to a Primates couple. The revelator even gives the date: reckoned from A.D. 1934, the first two human beings were born exactly 993,419 years ago (62:5.1). They had fully human thumbs and feet like those of modern man, they reached maturity at twelve, and they had a potential life span of about seventy-five years (62:5.2–5.3).

ch13:10.cap: Table 13.2  The Evolutionary Line Leading to Man
rows: Descended from the North American lemur type
Sprang from the dawn mammals; gave birth to superior twins
Humanlike hands and feet, upright posture, but not yet true human mind
True human beings; worshipful feelings; decisions of will

ch13:11: Even more decisive than the body was the difference that appeared in the emotions. The twins showed new emotions such as admiration and vanity, and they possessed some measure of sympathy and shame as well (62:5.4–5.5). Among these the revelator singles out the following as the most remarkable advance.
ch13:13: It is deeply significant that the first mark of man's humanity was the feeling of worship, before tools or language. In The Urantia Book man enters the scene as a being capable of turning toward God from the very beginning. Of course, this feeling was still mixed with ignorance and fear. The same paragraph adds that fear, joined with ignorance of natural phenomena, was about to give birth to primitive religion (62:5.4). The fact that the feeling of worship and the feeling of fear set out together gives rise, as we shall see, to the two branches of primitive religion. The story of the twins' parents also deserves mention. The mother gave her life trying to save the twins from an attack by gibbons, and the father, after his children had left, wandered about in grief until he died (62:5.10–5.11). The human race was born upon the sacrifice of animal mother love and father love.
ch13:14: 3. The Birth of Mind: The Seven Adjutant Mind-Spirits
ch13:15: What, then, changed animal mind into human mind? The Urantia Book explains the process as the successive functioning of the seven adjutant mind-spirits. The spirits of intuition, understanding, courage, knowledge, and counsel had functioned one after another in evolving animal life (62:6.3), and up through the Primates the activity of these five spirits grew steadily greater. But the two highest had not yet functioned (62:6.4). When the twins were about ten years old, the spirit of worship made contact first with the mind of the girl and then with that of the boy.

ch13:17.cap: Table 13.3  The Successive Functioning of the Adjutant Mind-Spirits and the Completion of Human Mind
rows: Reflex action; spontaneous association of ideas
The twins at about ten years of age
Mind contact of the worshipful feelings
The time of the decision to go north

ch13:18: This ministry did not begin suddenly. The Life Carriers bear witness to the long preparation of the adjutant spirits in these words.
ch13:20: As the brain grew, the ministry of mind deepened, and as the ministry of mind deepened, higher adjutant spirits were able to function. Material evolution and the ministry of mind rose side by side until, with the spirits of worship and wisdom, they crossed a single threshold. That threshold cannot be crossed by material forces alone, nor by the ministry of mind alone. Human mind is born at the meeting point of three things: the vessel of the brain, the ministry of the adjutant spirits, and the decision of the human being himself.
ch13:21: We must not miss the fact that the completion of mind and the act of decision occur at the same moment. Human mind comes not merely with the capacity to think but with the capacity to form purposes and to choose. The relationship of mind, personality, and will is treated in detail in Chapters 9 and 10.
ch13:22: 4. The First Decision and the Recognition of the Planet
ch13:23: At about nine years of age, by a river, the twins resolved to live with each other and for each other, and this was the beginning of a series of decisions that ended in their leaving for the north (62:5.8). The Life Carriers watched these decisions, but they did not make them for the twins.
ch13:25: Celestial beings can guide circumstances, but they cannot make the decisions of a mind in its place. This principle runs through the whole of human history. What the Life Carriers did was to lead the twins northward within the permissible limits of planetary function; the decision remained the twins' own to the end (62:5.9). On the third day after the twins fled, the first message from Salvington declared the meaning of their decision.
ch13:27: The decision of one pair opened a universe circuit. Urantia was formally recognized as a planet of human habitation 993,408 years ago (62:7.7), and with that the supervision of the Life Carriers came to an end. They record the reason in these words.
ch13:29: The mission of the Life Carriers lasts until will creatures appear. Once beings appear who are able to worship and to choose to ascend, what follows is left to their own choosing. When the twins were eleven years old, the message of the archangels gave a name to these parents of mankind.
ch13:31: 5. The Family of Andon: Fire, Clan, and Language
ch13:32: Andon signifies “the first Fatherlike creature to exhibit human perfection hunger” (63:0.3). It was not intelligence alone that led them to leave for the north. The revelator says that personality and the Adjuster lay beneath it.
ch13:34: On the way north Andon saw sparks fly from flint, and after two months of failures, when Fonta brought a dry bird's nest, the secret of kindling fire was solved (63:2.4–2.5). Fire became more than a skill of survival; it became a symbol of independence.
ch13:36: Their first child, Sontad, was born, and Andon and Fonta had nineteen children in all (63:3.1–3.2). This family possessed a marked clan consciousness and developed a vigorous language (63:4.6). The revelator finds the source of their solidarity in the ministry of mind.
ch13:38: The adjutant mind-spirits not only completed the minds of the twins; they also bound their family together. The men fought for their families and the women were devoted to their children. But this love did not yet reach beyond the immediate clan.

ch13:40.cap: Table 13.4  Chronology and Culture of the Andon Family
rows: Sontad born almost two years after their flight
Nineteen children, almost fifty grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren
Killed together in an earthquake at forty-two years of age
Kept together until the twentieth generation
Competition for food, social friction, and wars between clans

ch13:41: 6. Onagar and the First True Religion
ch13:42: As the Andonic clans scattered, their cultural and spiritual status retrogressed for nearly ten thousand years. Then Onagar arose, brought peace to the tribes, and led them together in the worship of the “Breath Giver to men and animals” (63:6.1). The prayer he taught expresses the very life and hopes of primitive man.
ch13:44: Onagar's emissaries were the world's first missionaries, and they carried the doctrine of one God and of the “Great Beyond” to remote settlements (63:6.7). Onagar established a system of tribal government that succeeding generations failed to attain for thousands of years, and until the Planetary Prince came there was never again so high a spiritual civilization (63:6.8). This religion was true because its faith answered to a real capacity within man. The Urantia Book speaks thus of all mortals who have indwelling Adjusters.
ch13:46: In the days of Onagar this potential was opened wide to mankind.

ch13:48.cap: Table 13.5  The Two Paths of Primitive Religion: Fear and Worship
rows: Natural phenomena such as thunder, lightning, rain, snow, and ice
The large food animals that sustained life made objects of worship
Ceremonies around revered animals that became the later sacrificial rites
Onagar's worship of one God and the concept of a life beyond

ch13:49: Andon and Fonta themselves were recognized in the adjudication at the arrival of the Planetary Prince, passed through the mansion worlds, became citizens of Jerusem, and there fused with their Adjusters (63:7.1–7.2). The first parents of mankind are also the first witnesses to eternal survival. They grieved over the betrayal of Caligastia and the failure of Adam, but they rejoiced greatly at the news that Michael had chosen their world as the scene of his final bestowal (63:7.1). The revelator closes their story in these words.
ch13:51: In Closing: A Human Race That Began with a Decision
ch13:52: The beginning of mankind as The Urantia Book portrays it follows a single logic. The Life Carriers designed life so that will would appear early. When the ministry of the adjutant mind-spirits reached worship and wisdom, human mind was complete, and the first decision of that mind opened a universe circuit and brought the recognition of the planet. The two who made that decision received personality and were indwelt by Adjusters; they gained fire and formed a family, and among their descendants true religion first blossomed. From the very beginning man was a being who chooses and worships. Yet the descendants of Andon scattered and retrogressed, and in their midst new races were to be born. The next chapter examines the origin and dispersion of the six colored races that sprang from the Sangik family.

ch13:53.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If the first mark that distinguishes man from the animal is the worshipful feelings (62:5.4) rather than tools or language, what does this tell us about the essential nature of man?
2. Even the Life Carriers could not control the minds of the twins (62:5.9). What does this teach us about the way God and the celestial beings treat human freedom?
3. The family of Andon had deep family affection, yet altruism was not yet born (63:4.3). How far does my own love reach today?

ch14:label: Chapter 14
ch14:title: The Origin and Dispersion of the Races
ch14:0: In the previous chapter mankind began with the decision of a single pair, Andon and Fonta. Yet the humanity of today is divided into many skin colors and many body types. Where did this diversity come from? The Urantia Book does not explain the origin of the races as an accident or a curse. The differentiation of the races is part of a plan for which the Life Carriers made provision from the beginning, and that plan extends to producing many races, scattering them, and then gathering them into one again. Following the text, this chapter asks in turn why the races arose, how they arose, where they were dispersed, and toward what they are moving.
ch14:1: 1. The Differentiation of the Races Is Part of the Plan
ch14:2: The need for racial differentiation first shows itself in the tendencies of evolving creatures. As the Andonic clans multiplied, contact between families gave rise to friction and feuds, and wars between the clans took away the most capable strains (63:4.7–4.8). The revelator tells us that the Life Carriers knew of this tendency beforehand.
ch14:4: On an ordinary evolutionary world these six races appear one after another in the order of the colors of the spectrum, beginning with the red man (52:1.1): the red man, the orange race, the yellow man, the green race, the blue man, and the indigo race. Of these the revelator calls the first, third, and fifth, the red, the yellow, and the blue, the primary races, and the other three the secondary races (51:4.3). But this differentiation is not merely a loss.
ch14:6: Differentiation is not an end in itself but a preparation for a greater synthesis. Because no single race can contain every potential, many races express differing potentials, and when these are later brought together again, mankind is enriched. This logic guides the whole chapter.

ch14:7.cap: Table 14.1  The Path of the Races on an Ordinary Evolutionary World
rows: Appear one after another in the order of the spectrum colors, beginning with the red man
Red, yellow, and blue are primary; orange, green, and indigo are secondary
The great age of racial dispersion under the Planetary Prince; color the basis of group formation
Improved by blending with the imported Adamic violet race
The races blended, color problems gone, all races of one blood

ch14:8: 2. The Dispersion and Retrogression of the Andonic Descendants
ch14:9: On Urantia this path began in a different order. The Andonic peoples existed before the colored races, and from about 950,000 years ago their descendants spread westward as far as France and England and eastward as far as Java (64:1.6). But their way was hemmed in from the beginning. To the east lay the Tibetan highlands, to the south and west the Mediterranean, which then extended to the Indian Ocean, and to the north the ice sheets (64:1.1). The revelator says that this situation became one root of religious feeling.
ch14:11: Even so, the progressive Andonites did not turn back to their tree-dwelling relatives in the south. The revelator points out that this choice was the condition that divided progress from retrogression.
ch14:13: But the groups that went east mingled with their inferior animal cousins, and as that mixture in turn combined with the Andonites of the north, the settlements that worshiped the Breath Giver dwindled (64:1.7). Meanwhile some groups preserved the heritage of Andon and Onagar. The Foxhall peoples of England passed on the working of flint to later ages and became the ancestors of the Eskimos (64:2.5), and the Badonan tribes of the northwestern highlands of India were the only descendants of Andon who did not practice human sacrifice (64:3.1). The Neanderthal races that sprang from the Badonan stock dominated the world for almost half a million years, but on the whole their era was a time of retrogression. The Neanderthalers had no religion beyond a shameful superstition, and they even sacrificed human beings to appease the invisible forces (64:4.12). The revelator assesses that period in these words.

ch14:15.cap: Table 14.2  The Principal Branches of the Andonic Descendants
rows: Preserved comparatively much of Andonic culture; ancestors of the Eskimos
The only Andonic descendants who did not offer human sacrifice
A somewhat superior and highly prolific people
From France to China and North Africa
Excellent fighters; no religion beyond superstition

ch14:16: 3. The Sangik Family: Six Races from One Family
ch14:17: The new races came out of the midst of this retrogression. Five hundred thousand years ago, after long wars among the Badonan tribes, about one hundred families remained, and these survivors were the most intelligent and desirable of the descendants of Andon and Fonta then living (64:5.1). And among them something unexpected happened.
ch14:19: The nineteen children of the Sangik family had skins that turned different colors on exposure to sunlight. Five were red, two orange, four yellow, two green, four blue, and two indigo, and when they mated within their tribe, their offspring tended toward the skin color of the Sangik parent (64:5.3). The revelator explains this event by comparison with ordinary worlds.
ch14:21: The races that on other worlds arise one by one through mutations in different lines were born on Urantia as brothers and sisters. However great the differences between the races, their root is a single household. And that household goes back in turn to Andon and Fonta. Because the Sangik family came from the Badonan stock, the best of the Andonic descendants, all the colored races are in the end descendants of the first two human beings. It is also worth remembering that the Planetary Prince arrived at this time (64:5.4). The second great chapter of human history begins where the birth of the six races and the arrival of the Prince coincide.
ch14:22: 4. The Characteristics and Leaders of the Six Sangik Races
ch14:23: As the revelator describes the characteristics of the six races one by one, he records both what they gained and what they lost. The red man was the first to develop tribal civilization and government (64:6.3); the yellow man was the first to abandon the chase and achieve a settled life based on agriculture (64:6.14); and the blue man early invented the spear and laid the foundations of many of the arts of modern civilization (64:6.21). The explanation of why the yellow man survived shows on what the destiny of a race depends.
ch14:25: Of the red, green, and orange races, by contrast, the text records this: “These three races virtually destroyed themselves before they were finally all but annihilated by their enemies of other races” (64:7.7). It was peace, rather than strength, that preserved a race. The blue man, moreover, is described as having “the brain power of the red man associated with the soul and sentiment of the yellow man” (64:6.21), and he was the race the Adamic descendants preferred above all. As the table below shows, each of the six races had a leader who taught them anew about God.

ch14:26.cap: Table 14.3  The Characteristics and Spiritual Leaders of the Six Sangik Races
rows: First tribal civilization and government; monogamy
An urge to build anything and everything
First settled agriculture; social organization and cooperation
Weakened by migrations in different directions
Invention of the spear; foundations of the arts of civilization
The last to leave the homeland; went to Africa

ch14:27: Most of these leaders appeared in the dark ages that followed the rebellion of Caligastia. Besides the renowned leaders, the revelator does not forget the share of countless lesser teachers.
ch14:29: The text does not conceal the differences in ability among the races. But it also makes clear that these differences are not differences in spiritual status. Of the indigo race, which it describes as the least advanced, the revelator adds this.
ch14:31: Biologic endowment and cultural achievement differ from race to race, but standing before God is the same. This distinction is the most important link in the logic of this chapter. Race belongs to the level of body and civilization; the relationship with God belongs to the level of personality and the Adjuster.
ch14:33: Why, then, three or six races rather than one? The revelator says that there are reasons worth noting even if mortals cannot fully appreciate them all, and he gives five (64:6.30).

ch14:34.cap: Table 14.4  Five Reasons for Evolving Several Colored Races
rows: Variety is needed for the differential survival of superior strains
The crossing of superior races can produce stronger and more vigorous races
Diversity among the races stimulates wholesome competition
Differences in status develop human tolerance and altruism
Homogeneity is not desirable before high spiritual levels are attained

ch14:35: The fourth and fifth reasons are especially striking. In the words of the text, they read as follows.
ch14:38: Diversity gives man a place to learn tolerance and altruism, and becoming one is desirable only after spiritual maturity has first been reached. In the previous chapter we saw that altruism was not yet born in the family of Andon (63:4.3). The differences between the races become the very soil in which that altruism grows. Racial diversity is also a school for man's moral growth.
ch14:39: 6. Dispersion, Blending, and the Violet Race
ch14:40: Hemmed in by the ice, the Sangik races lived intermingled in the foothills for almost one hundred thousand years, and from early times a natural antipathy appeared between the different races (64:7.2). The superior primary races avoided the tropics and went north, while the secondary races were drawn south into Africa (64:7.3). The orange race was absorbed or exterminated by the green, and the green by the indigo (64:6.13, 64:7.14). But dispersion was also mingling. The blue men who went to Europe met there the Neanderthalers, descendants of their common ancestor Andon (64:7.9).
ch14:42: In the text, blending is in itself neither good nor bad. Again and again civilization deteriorated when superior stocks mingled with inferior ones (64:1.8), and when superior stocks came in, the older races were improved. The result of blending depends on what is mingled with what. This principle will later be the key to understanding the mission of Adam. When the migrations ended, the map looked like this.
ch14:44: From then on the humanity of Urantia became the result of a blending and reblending of five basic stocks (81:4.1). The revelator says that to understand the races of today one must take into account the influence of the Adamic stock that came later (64:7.12). On ordinary worlds the violet race of the planetary Adam and Eve blends with the evolutionary races and upsteps them. On Urantia, however, this plan was not extensively carried out (51:4.4). The mission of Adam and its setback are treated in Chapter 16.

ch14:45.cap: Table 14.5  The Five Basic Stocks That Make Up the Humanity of Urantia
rows: The red, yellow, and blue races
The orange, green, and indigo races

ch14:46: On the way to that goal the revelator calls not only for biologic blending but for ethical awakening.
ch14:48: Toward what, then, does the history of the races move? On normal and loyal worlds the path of the races reaches the following state.
ch14:50: The Life Carrier who recorded this long history does not look down on our primitive ancestors. He honors their struggles in these words.
ch14:52: In Closing: From One Household to One Blood
ch14:53: The doctrine of the races traces a circle. The Life Carriers provided for the separation of the races so that man, the descendant of fighting animals, could live together. The six colored races of Urantia were born as brothers and sisters in a single family, the Sangik family, and scattered over the world, each with its own characteristics and achievements. Those differences served natural selection, competition, and tolerance; they did not divide standing before God. And that dispersion was planned to lead at last to a world in which all races are of one blood and the brotherhood of man flourishes. On Urantia, however, this plan suffered two great setbacks. The next chapter examines the first of them, the Lucifer rebellion and the betrayal of Caligastia.

ch14:54.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. The six colored races were born as brothers and sisters in one family (64:5.2). What does this fact ask of the way I look at race today?
2. Why is it important to hold together both the differences in ability among the races and their equal standing “before the celestial powers” (64:6.27)?
3. If differences among the races are essential to the development of tolerance and altruism (64:6.34), what kind of school are the differences around me becoming for me?

ch15:label: Chapter 15
ch15:title: The Lucifer Rebellion
ch15:0: The previous two chapters followed the process by which mankind was born and dispersed according to plan. From this chapter on we turn to the setbacks that shook that plan. The first setback began not with man but in heaven. Lucifer, the sovereign of the system of Satania, raised a rebellion, and Caligastia, the Planetary Prince of Urantia, joined in it. In The Urantia Book this event is not merely an old story; it is a place of doctrine that discloses the nature of evil, sin, and liberty. This chapter asks three questions. How does a being created perfect come to rebellion? What was false about the liberty the rebel proclaimed? And why did God not destroy the rebels at once?
ch15:2: Lucifer was a brilliant primary Lanonandek Son of Nebadon, designated as one of the one hundred most able and brilliant personalities among more than seven hundred thousand of his kind (53:0.1). The system of Satania that he ruled contains 607 inhabited worlds (53:1.1). The revelator sets his brilliant beginning and his end side by side in a single sentence.
ch15:4: This sentence is like an anatomy of rebellion. The urge of self, the rejection of allegiance, the disregard of fraternal obligations, blindness to cosmic relationships, and the sophistry of spurious liberty are set out in order. Lucifer's first assistant was Satan, and the being commonly called the devil on Urantia was Caligastia, the deposed Planetary Prince (53:1.4). In all the history of the Lanonandek Sons only three System Sovereigns have held the government of the Creator Son in contempt (53:0.2). Rebellion is not common in the universe, and for that very reason this event left a deep and peculiar mark on Urantia. One more thing must be remembered: the rebels were not created evil from the beginning. All of them were Sons of God of high position and outstanding ability, and it was in the very midst of that excellence that they fell.

ch15:5.cap: Table 15.1  The Principal Personalities of the Rebellion
rows: Primary Lanonandek Son; Sovereign of the system of Satania
Leader of the rebellion; proclaimed the Declaration of Liberty
Secondary Lanonandek; Planetary Prince of Urantia
Betrayed the planet; called the devil
Chief executive of the Urantia rebels

ch15:7: The cause of the rebellion cannot be sought outside. There were no special conditions in the system of Satania that would have provoked rebellion, and the revelator believes that Lucifer would have fomented rebellion wherever he had been (53:2.2).
ch15:9: What nourished that idea was pride. Lucifer deceived himself until he came to believe that his rebellion was at least for the good of the system.
ch15:11: The same paragraph says that at some point in this experience he became insincere, and evil evolved into deliberate and willful sin. Here the distinction The Urantia Book draws between evil and sin becomes important. At the opening of Paper 54 the revelator sets out four terms.

ch15:13.cap: Table 15.2  The Distinction of Error, Evil, Sin, and Iniquity
rows: Partial realization of, or maladjustment to, universe realities
Open and persistent defiance of recognized reality

ch15:14: Caligastia walked the same road. He was an extreme individualist and was restless under authority (66:8.1). Lucifer and Caligastia had been patiently instructed and lovingly warned about their critical tendencies and their pride, but they misconstrued all such help as unwarranted criticism and infringement of their liberty (66:8.2). Rebellion does not happen overnight. A little pride leads to the rejection of counsel, rejection breeds self-deception, and self-deception hardens into willful sin. Of Caligastia the revelator adds that by this deliberate sin he so completely distorted his personality that his mind has never since fully regained its equilibrium (67:1.3). Sin destroys not only outward order but the very personality that chooses it. Repeated sin becomes habit, and the habitual sinner easily falls into iniquity (67:1.6).
ch15:16: The trouble in Lucifer's mind at last took form as the Lucifer Declaration of Liberty. The cause of the rebels was stated under three heads (53:3.1).

ch15:17.cap: Table 15.3  The Three Claims of the Lucifer Manifesto
rows: 1. The reality of the Universal Father
The Father does not exist and is a myth invented by the Paradise Sons; denial that personality is the gift of the Father
The local systems should be autonomous; the interference of the Ancients of Days is tyranny
3. The attack on the ascension plan
Too much time and energy are spent on training mortals; ascenders should enjoy the liberty of self-determination

ch15:18: The three claims lead back to a single root. The first denies the Father, the second denies the rule of the Son who represents the Father, and the third denies the very path to the Father. If there is no Father, there is no one to be loyal to and no goal of ascension. All that is left is self-determination. Denial of the reality of God is the starting point of false liberty. As the third claim shows, Lucifer mocked the long plan of training for ascending mortals as a fiction. Yet that plan is the very will of the Father, who intends that creatures of time should attain perfection through experience. As a result of the rebellion the system was isolated from its sister systems (67:3.1), and the “war in heaven” spread to every planet of Satania. That war was not a war of swords and weapons but a struggle of minds and loyalties.
ch15:21: The revelator says that of all the problems the rebellion left behind, none has caused more difficulty than the inability of immature mortals to distinguish between true and false liberty (54:1.1). So he states again and again the conditions of liberty.

ch15:24.cap: Table 15.4  True Liberty and False Liberty
rows: The deception of the error of time and the evil of space
Exploitation of others and unjust power

ch15:25: What, then, was Lucifer's crime? He cried out for liberty, but in fact he sought to take away the liberty of other beings. God gave free will to every personal creature so that each might take part in the long struggle of evolution and contribute his own share (54:2.3).
ch15:28: False liberty in the end steals the liberty of others. That is why the revelator says that the Lucifer manifesto, dressed in the garments of liberty, stands forth in the light of reason as a threat to consummate the “theft of personal liberty and to do it on a scale that has been approached only twice in all the history of Nebadon.” (54:2.3). Why, then, did God not make from the beginning only beings who could not sin? The revelator's answer is clear. If freedom of choice is real, the possibility of wrong choice must also be real.
ch15:30: The Gods neither create evil nor permit sin and rebellion (54:0.2). But wherever there are imperfect beings endowed with free will, there is the possibility of sin. What God safeguards is not sin but liberty. What Lucifer sought to take away, God preserves to the end.
ch15:31: 5. The Betrayal of Urantia and the Loyalty of Amadon
ch15:32: Caligastia had agreed beforehand to betray the planet once the rebellion was proclaimed (67:1.2). The revelator regards this betrayal as the gravest of evils, for no trust is more sacred than that of a Planetary Prince.
ch15:34: Yet on the same planet there was also the opposite choice. Forty members of the Prince's staff of one hundred, including Van, refused to join the rebellion (67:3.2), and Amadon, a descendant of Andon and Fonta, stood firmly by Van's side throughout the seven years of struggle (67:3.8).
ch15:36: It was not the size of the intellect that decided loyalty. Van's loyalty was the product of clear thinking, sincere motivation, unselfish purpose, and the unquestioning dedication of himself to the doing of the Father's will (67:3.6). For seven years the first question of all subordinate celestial life was “What of Amadon of Urantia, does he still stand unmoved?” (67:8.3). After the rebellion Van's followers withdrew to the highlands west of India and planned the rehabilitation of the world, and the descendants of Amadon became the biologic leaven that supplied leadership through the long dark ages after the rebellion (67:6.1, 67:6.3). The revelator says that the loyalty of Amadon and his associates achieved so much good that it cannot be exceeded even by the sum total of all the evil and sorrow of the Lucifer rebellion (67:8.4). And though the presence of Caligastia became one ground of the doctrine of a devil, the teaching that he could move the human will by force was fiction (66:8.6).
ch15:38: This passage is the most direct comfort the doctrine of rebellion offers to man. Even a fallen Prince could not coerce the human will, and even the Adjuster does not compel it. The destiny of man depends in the end on man's own choice.
ch15:39: 6. Why Were They Not Destroyed at Once?
ch15:40: The hardest question remains. Why did God allow the rebels to do harm for so long? From the beginning of the rebellion Michael offered every rebel forgiveness and restoration to service upon repentance (53:9.1). And he delayed the execution of justice. The revelator says that those who have become parents can better understand why a Creator-father is so slow to condemn his sons (54:4.2).
ch15:42: That delay belongs to the very nature of mercy.

ch15:45.cap: Table 15.5  Some Reasons Why the Rebels Were Not Immediately Interned
rows: Gives the wrongdoer time to formulate a fully chosen attitude
An affectionate father is never in haste to administer punishment
Not having completed his bestowals, he did not exercise summary jurisdiction
That every creature might fully mature a choice regarding the issues of rebellion
Exposing sin rather than hiding it is the quickest cure

ch15:46: We are told that on Uversa as many as forty-eight reasons are taught for permitting evil to run the full course of its own moral bankruptcy and spiritual extinction (54:5.14). The result is astonishing. From a rebellion that at first appeared to be an unmitigated calamity, benefits gradually began to accrue. The sum of evil continued to increase only on certain isolated worlds, while the beneficial repercussions extended out through the universe and superuniverse, even to Havona (54:6.6). The benefits of rebellion, of course, do not go to the rebels. Good cannot come out of evil to those who plan and do evil, but all things work together for good to those who love to do the will of God (54:4.7).
ch15:48: And however wide the damage of rebellion may be, there is a boundary it cannot cross. The outward repercussions of sin are collective, but its spiritual consequences are thoroughly personal (67:7.1–7.2).
ch15:50: In Closing: Liberty Is Liberty Only Within Reality
ch15:51: The doctrine of the Lucifer rebellion is held together by a single logic. Rebellion began not outside but in the pride within one personality's mind, and through self-deception it became willful sin. That sin came to light in a manifesto denying the reality of the Father, and while it cried out for liberty, it in fact sought to steal the liberty of every creature. True liberty exists only in relationship with reality and with divinity. God did not destroy the rebels at once but gave a time of mercy, and within that time loyalty such as Amadon's shone forth and the good resulting from the rebellion came to exceed the evil a thousandfold. The rebellion has ended on Jerusem, and it ends on the fallen worlds as fast as divine Sons arrive (53:9.7). But Urantia was isolated by this rebellion, and in that isolation the second setback came. The next chapter examines the mission of Adam and Eve and their default.

ch15:52.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If no one ever suggested rebellion to Lucifer and the idea had its origin in his own mind (53:2.3), how can I recognize in my own life the process by which pride grows into self-deception?
2. In the light of the words “True liberty is the fruit of self-control” (54:1.6), what among the things I regard as liberty is in fact nothing more than self-assertion?
3. What does the reason Amadon, lacking both intellect and experience, could remain loyal to the end (67:3.6, 67:3.9) teach me in the places where I waver today?

ch16:label: Chapter 16
ch16:title: Adam and Eve
ch16:sub: The Mission of Biologic Uplift and Its Default
ch16:0: What the Lucifer rebellion left on Urantia was isolation and confusion. Into the midst of that confusion came Adam and Eve, a Material Son and Daughter of God. Their story has long been handed down under the name of the fall of man. The Urantia Book, however, reads this story in an entirely different way. Adam and Eve were not ancestors who plunged mankind into a curse; they were emissaries sent to uplift mankind biologically. This chapter asks: Who are the Material Sons and Daughters, and what do they come to do? Why did their mission miscarry on Urantia? And what did that default leave to mankind?
ch16:1: 1. The Material Sons and Daughters of God
ch16:2: The Material Sons and Daughters are the offspring of a Creator Son, beings destined to function as physical uplifters on the evolutionary worlds (51:1.1). They are from eight to ten feet tall, their bodies give off a violet radiance, and they maintain their immortality by a dual nutrition, taking certain universe energies directly along with material food (51:1.3–1.4). Unlike the other celestial sons, they are visible to mortals and can actually mingle with them (51:1.7). The revelator sums up their place in a single phrase: they are “the connecting links between the spiritual and physical worlds” (51:1.6).

ch16:3.cap: Table 16.1  The Nature of the Material Sons and Daughters
rows: Offspring of the Creator Son; the Universe Mother Spirit does not participate
Eight to ten feet tall; violet radiance; male and female equal and complemental
Dual nutrition of material food and universe energies
Do not possess Adjusters while on the system capitals and on planetary missions
Visible to mortals and able to mingle and procreate with them

ch16:4: The purpose for which they come to the evolutionary worlds is clear.
ch16:6: 2. The Adamic Plan on a Normal World
ch16:7: On an ordinary world this mission is not hurried. Adam and Eve first remain biologically segregated from the evolutionary mortals for many generations while they build up a strong race of their order. This is the origin of the violet race (51:3.3). The violet race does not blend with the natives until its numbers exceed one million (51:5.2), and Adam and Eve themselves never mate with the evolutionary races; biologic improvement is the task of their offspring (51:5.3). The six colored races we saw in an earlier chapter were destined to be blended and upstepped through this very amalgamation (51:4.8). The revelator portrays the result when the plan is carried out in these words.

ch16:9.cap: Table 16.2  The Order of the Adamic Mission on a Normal World
rows: Adam and Eve build up the violet race for many generations
No amalgamation until the violet race exceeds one million
The Prince's staff brings superior men and women to the garden; voluntary mating
Those who mate with the Adamic offspring pledge themselves to monogamy
In one hundred thousand years, more progress than in a million years

ch16:10: The heart of this plan is patience and order. First a pure stock is fully established, and then those who have been selected are allowed to take part voluntarily. It is a method that honors the slow pace of evolution while adding to it a gift that comes from above.
ch16:12: Urantia was not a normal world. The Life Carriers, seeing that the biologic progress of the races was nearing its peak, petitioned for a Material Son, and less than one hundred years after the inspection Adam and Eve arrived (73:0.1, 73:0.3). But what they met was a planet retarded by rebellion and placed under spiritual isolation. The races were biologically fit, yet their defective strains had never been purged (75:1.2); the people were wholly unprepared to accept the brotherhood of man, and their speech was scattered among hundreds of dialects (75:1.3).
ch16:14: They were, moreover, isolated. After the Melchizedek receivers left early, there was no way to consult their superiors (75:1.4). For more than a hundred years of effort, the world outside the Garden scarcely improved (75:0.1). The revelator points out in advance where their failure would come from.
ch16:17: Caligastia visited the Garden often, but Adam and Eve were adamant against his proposals of compromise. And here the revelator confirms again a principle from the previous chapter: “neither Caligastia nor his associate had power to influence any individual against his will” (75:2.1). So the fallen Prince gave up on Adam and attempted a flank attack upon Eve (75:2.3). His channel was Serapatatia, a leader of the Nodites. Serapatatia sincerely sympathized with Adam's cause and was wholly honest, but he could not wait for the time it would take to build up the violet race fully.
ch16:19: Serapatatia's proposal was to give the Nodites a leader partly of violet origin and so bind them more closely to the Garden (75:3.5). Following this plan, which had matured over more than five years, Eve met with Cano, a Nodite leader, and consented to add her own little plan for saving the world to the divine plan (75:3.7–3.9). Solonia, the voice in the Garden, defines the character of that act in these words.
ch16:22: This principle, that good motives do not justify evil methods, is the doctrinal heart of the story of Adam. Adam's choice was of a different character. On the day after Eve's misstep he sought out Laotta, a Nodite woman, and committed the same folly.
ch16:24: This choice of Adam's was an error of judgment, but its motive was a supermortal affection for his mate. He could not endure the thought of spending the years on Urantia alone without Eve (75:5.2). Yet the consequences of the default did not stop with those who committed it. The enraged dwellers of the Garden destroyed a nearby Nodite settlement, and Serapatatia, in remorse, took his own life (75:5.3–5.4). The revelator records on whom that sorrow fell.
ch16:26: Soon an army of the Nodites marched upon the Garden. The Melchizedeks refused to advise Adam and told him only to do as he thought best (75:6.1). The principle that heaven does not intervene in human choice was kept even at this moment. And Adam made one more decision.

ch16:28.cap: Table 16.3  The Course of Events Leading to the Default
rows: Caligastia makes a flank attack upon Eve instead of Adam
Serapatatia, a Nodite leader, sincere but impatient
To produce a Nodite leader of violet blood and bind the Nodites to the Garden
Secret conference with Cano; adding her own plan to the divine plan
Deliberately chose to share the fate of Eve
Destruction of a Nodite settlement; long wars between Adamites and Nodites

ch16:29: 5. The Verdict: Default, but Not Rebellion
ch16:30: Gabriel pronounced the verdict. The Adam and Eve of Urantia were adjudged in default, having violated the covenant of their trusteeship (75:7.1). But the judges of Salvington exonerated them of the charge of contempt for the universe government (75:7.2). They were reduced to the status of mortals, and access to the energies stored in the tree of life was denied them (75:7.3, 75:7.6). The revelator makes the meaning of this verdict clear.
ch16:32: The distinction drawn in the previous chapter applies here exactly. Eve's act was a misadaptation of plans, that is, evil. Lucifer's rebellion was a purposeful resistance to divine reality, that is, sin. Accordingly, their outcomes also differ. In the second garden Adam and Eve were informed that their repentance had been accepted. Their transgression was an error of judgment, not deliberate rebellion (76:5.1). And to them, now mortals, something happened that had never happened before.
ch16:34: The Adjusters they had not possessed as Material Sons entered them once they became mortals. Their reduction in status was at the same time the beginning of a new path. Adam lived 530 years, and on the third day after his death he was awakened, together with Eve, in a special resurrection (76:5.5, 76:6.2). They passed through the worlds of ascension and reached Jerusem.

ch16:36.cap: Table 16.4  The Consequences Experienced by Adam and Eve
rows: Reduced from Material Sons to mortals
Access to the energies of the tree of life denied, leading to the dissolution of the mortal body
Two thirds of the children of the age of choice, and all the younger children, went to Edentia
Exonerated of the charge of rebellion; adjudged in default only
Repentance, Adjuster indwelling, special resurrection, return to Jerusem as ascendant citizens

ch16:38: Was mankind, then, cursed because of Adam? The answer of The Urantia Book is emphatic.
ch16:40: Adam and Eve fell from the status of Material Sons to that of mortals, but that was not the fall of mankind (75:8.1). The revelator directly removes the old charge laid against Adam.
ch16:42: Failure and contribution are present together in one man. The Urantia Book neither dresses Adam up as a hero nor brands him a sinner. Even in the second garden Adam strove to leave behind his life plasm, and through it 1,570 superior men and women were added to the world (76:4.8). Afterward the violet race spread into world civilization through the Andites. But because the plan miscarried early, mankind received only a small share. The revelator connects that result with the fear that people experience today.
ch16:44: Weak resistance to disease comes from the same cause (76:4.7). The setback is real, but it is not inherited guilt; it is a gift received in lesser measure. And the empty place left by that lesser gift must now be filled by human effort. The revelator says that Urantia, having failed to achieve racial harmony through the Adamic technique, must solve the problem of race improvement by other, largely human, methods (51:5.7).

ch16:45.cap: Table 16.5  The Doctrine of the Fall and the Understanding of The Urantia Book
rows: There was no fall of man; mankind was uplifted
Is Adam the cause of a curse?
The cause of a curse on the human race
He should not be regarded as the cause of a curse
The moral guilt of sin is wholly personal
Repentance, resurrection, and ascendant citizenship on Jerusem

ch16:46: The story of Adam leaves a lesson for everyone who ascends.
ch16:48: Yet misfortune was not the whole destiny of Urantia. Because the failure of Adam and the rebellion of Caligastia plunged this planet into darkness, that very darkness became the background against which Michael chose this world as the arena of his bestowal (76:5.7). The revelator writes.
ch16:50: In Closing: A Mission of Patience
ch16:51: The doctrine of Adam and Eve unfolds in this way. The Material Sons and Daughters come as a gift of physical grace to uplift the evolutionary races biologically. Their mission is a plan of patience that builds up a pure stock and waits for voluntary participation. On Urantia they met the most difficult conditions; Eve chose a wrong method from good motives, and Adam, out of love, shared her fate. It was evil but not rebellion, and to them, once they repented, the way of the Adjuster, resurrection, and ascension was opened. Mankind did not fall but was instead uplifted. And the revelator reads all these mistakes as a sign of a universe in which personality rules: “Perfection is our eternal goal, not our origin” (75:8.6). After Adam the spiritual darkness deepened, and the light of truth was in danger of going out. The next chapter examines Machiventa Melchizedek, who came to keep that light alive, and the world-wide spread of his teachings.

ch16:52.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If Eve's default represented “the wrong way to achieve righteous ends” (75:4.6), when have I tried with good intentions to circumvent the divine way?
2. Adjusters indwelt Adam and Eve only after they had become mortals (76:5.2). What does this tell us about the experience of failure and repentance?
3. How does the teaching that there was no “fall of man” (75:8.2) change the way I look at myself and at mankind?
